projects.name: Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
A new analytics dashboard that unifies three data streams: (1) customer CSV files, (2) application log files, and (3) interactive visualization components. Deliverables include a resilient CSV ingestion pipeline, a log parsing/aggregation service, a reusable chart component library, and an assembled dashboard application with tests and deployment tooling.

Structure: 5 milestones, each decomposed into executable tasks sized so no single task exceeds a complexity of 6/10.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-pipeline, visualization

tasks.name: Milestone 1: Customer CSV Ingestion Pipeline
tasks.details:
Build the pipeline that turns raw customer CSV exports into clean, queryable records.

Scope:
- Define and document the canonical customer schema (fields, types, nullability).
- Implement a streaming CSV reader with encoding/delimiter detection.
- Add validation, normalization, and row-level error handling with a rejects file.
- Load cleaned records into the dashboard's storage layer idempotently.

Exit criteria: A messy real customer CSV can be ingested end-to-end, with invalid rows quarantined and a reconciliation report showing row counts. Decomposed into tasks 1.1-1.4; no child task exceeds complexity 6.

tasks.name: Milestone 2: Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details:
Turn raw application log files into structured events and aggregate metrics the dashboard can chart.

Scope:
- Specify the log event schema and the supported log formats.
- Implement a parser that handles multi-line stack traces and mixed timestamps.
- Aggregate into time-bucketed metrics (error rate, request volume, latency percentiles).
- Persist aggregates for fast dashboard queries.

Exit criteria: A representative log archive is parsed with an unparsed-line rate under 1%, and hourly aggregates are queryable. Decomposed into tasks 2.1-2.4; no child task exceeds complexity 6.

tasks.name: Milestone 3: Visualization Component Library
tasks.details:
Create the reusable chart and widget components the dashboard screens are built from.

Scope:
- Establish the design tokens (color palette, typography, spacing) shared by all charts.
- Build the core chart primitives: time series, bar, and distribution charts.
- Build composite widgets: KPI tile, filter bar, and data table with sorting.
- Cover accessibility and responsive behavior.

Exit criteria: A component storybook/preview page renders every primitive and widget against fixture data at three breakpoints. Decomposed into tasks 3.1-3.4; no child task exceeds complexity 6.

tasks.name: Milestone 4: Dashboard Application Assembly
tasks.details:
Assemble the ingestion outputs, log metrics, and chart components into the actual dashboard application.

Scope:
- Implement the query/API layer that serves aggregates to the UI.
- Compose dashboard screens (customer overview, log health, combined view).
- Wire up global filters (date range, segment) and shareable URL state.
- Add loading, empty, and error states.

Exit criteria: All three screens load real ingested data, filters apply across every widget, and the URL reproduces a filtered view. Decomposed into tasks 4.1-4.4; no child task exceeds complexity 6.

tasks.name: Milestone 5: Testing, Deployment & Documentation
tasks.details:
Harden and ship: automated tests, CI, deployment, and operator documentation.

Scope:
- Unit/integration tests for parsers, aggregations, and API contracts.
- End-to-end smoke test on a seeded dataset.
- CI pipeline with build, lint, and test gates.
- Deployment configuration plus a runbook and data dictionary.

Exit criteria: CI is green on main, a one-command deploy reaches staging, and a new engineer can onboard from the runbook alone. Decomposed into tasks 5.1-5.4; no child task exceeds complexity 6.

tasks.name: 1.1 Define canonical customer schema & data dictionary
tasks.details:
Deliverable: a written schema spec plus a machine-readable schema file (e.g. JSON Schema / Pydantic model) describing every customer field.

Work:
- Inventory the columns present across a sample of real customer CSV exports; note variations in naming and order.
- For each field define type, nullability, allowed values/enums, and example values.
- Identify PII fields and mark them for masking or exclusion.
- Document keys: which fields uniquely identify a customer and which are slowly-changing attributes.

Done when: the schema file is committed, the data dictionary section is written, and a reviewer has signed off on PII classification.

tasks.name: 1.2 Build streaming CSV reader with encoding & delimiter detection
tasks.details:
Deliverable: a reusable reader module that yields typed row batches without loading whole files into memory.

Work:
- Detect encoding (UTF-8 / UTF-8-BOM / Latin-1) and delimiter automatically with an explicit override option.
- Stream in configurable batch sizes (target: 500MB file with flat memory usage).
- Handle quoted fields, embedded newlines, and trailing-empty-column quirks.
- Emit a header-mapping report so renamed columns resolve to the canonical schema from task 1.1.
- Surface malformed-record positions (line numbers) to the caller instead of throwing away context.

Done when: unit tests cover at least 8 fixture variations (BOM, CRLF, semicolon, quoted newlines, ragged rows) and a large-file smoke run stays within the memory budget.

tasks.name: 1.3 Implement validation, normalization & rejects handling
tasks.details:
Deliverable: a validation stage that converts raw rows into schema-conformant records or quarantines them with a reason.

Work:
- Type coercion and normalization: trim whitespace, normalize dates to ISO-8601 UTC, canonicalize country/segment enums, strip currency formatting from numeric fields.
- Row-level validation against the schema with a stable error code per failure type.
- Write rejected rows to a rejects file that includes the original row plus error code, field, and source line.
- Policy decision: drop vs. flag-and-keep for soft failures (e.g. missing optional field) — document the choice.
- Mask or drop PII fields identified in task 1.1.

Done when: a fixture set with known-bad rows produces exactly the expected rejects file and no unhandled exceptions.

tasks.name: 1.4 Idempotent load into storage + reconciliation report
tasks.details:
Deliverable: the loader that writes cleaned records into the dashboard's storage layer, plus a per-run reconciliation report.

Work:
- Upsert semantics keyed on the customer key from task 1.1 so re-running a file is a no-op (no duplicates).
- Batch writes with a transaction per batch so a failure leaves no partial batch committed.
- Produce a run report: rows read, rows accepted, rows rejected (by error code), rows inserted vs. updated, duration.
- Make the run re-runnable from an arbitrary batch offset after a crash.

Done when: running the same file twice leaves record counts unchanged and the reconciliation report totals match the input row count.

tasks.name: 2.1 Define log event schema & supported formats
tasks.details:
Deliverable: a log event schema plus a documented list of formats the pipeline guarantees to support.

Work:
- Collect samples of each log source (app server, worker, access log, error log) and record their line formats.
- Define the normalized event shape: timestamp (UTC), level, service, host, request_id, message, stack_trace, latency_ms, status_code, plus an `unparsed` fallback.
- Decide handling for JSON logs vs. plain-text/grok patterns.
- Specify how timezone offsets and naive local timestamps are resolved.
- State explicitly what is out of scope (e.g. binary logs).

Done when: the schema is committed and every sampled log source has a documented mapping to it, including known gaps.

tasks.name: 2.2 Build log parser incl. multi-line stack traces & timestamp normalization
tasks.details:
Deliverable: a parser that converts raw log lines into normalized events per the task 2.1 schema.

Work:
- Line-oriented parser with pluggable format matchers (JSON, regex/grok, fallback).
- Reassemble multi-line stack traces and continuation lines into the parent event instead of emitting them as noise.
- Normalize timestamps to UTC ISO-8601; record the original string for auditability.
- Extract request_id so related lines can be correlated.
- Count unparsed lines and keep a capped sample of them for debugging rather than silently dropping.

Done when: parsing a representative log archive yields an unparsed rate under 1%, stack traces attach to their parent event, and golden-file tests pass.

tasks.name: 2.3 Implement time-bucketed aggregation metrics
tasks.details:
Deliverable: an aggregation module producing the metrics the dashboard charts.

Work:
- Time-bucket events at 1-minute and 1-hour granularity with a configurable window.
- Compute: request volume, error rate (by level and status class), p50/p95/p99 latency, top-N error messages, and unique request_id counts.
- Handle counter semantics correctly (rate vs. raw count) and align bucket boundaries to the window start.
- Guard against the known percentile pitfall: store histogram buckets, not just a precomputed p95, so windows can be merged.
- Emit an aggregate record keyed by (bucket_start, service, granularity).

Done when: aggregates recomputed from a fixed fixture log match hand-verified expected values, including percentile merge across two adjacent windows.

tasks.name: 2.4 Persist aggregates for fast dashboard queries
tasks.details:
Deliverable: an incremental ingestion job that writes aggregates into a query-friendly store.

Work:
- Upsert aggregate rows idempotently so re-processing an overlapping log range does not double-count.
- Design the read path: a single indexed query must return a 30-day hourly series in under 500ms on representative volume.
- Add retention/rollup policy (raw events kept short-term, hourly aggregates kept long-term).
- Add a backfill command to recompute a date range after a parser fix.

Done when: re-running an overlapping range leaves totals unchanged, and the 30-day series query meets the latency target in a benchmark.

tasks.name: 3.1 Define chart design tokens & theming
tasks.details:
Deliverable: a shared token layer every chart consumes, so colors and spacing are never hardcoded per component.

Work:
- Define a categorical palette plus semantic colors (success/warning/error) that remain distinguishable for color-vision deficiency.
- Define typography scale, axis/gridline weights, spacing increments, and border-radius values.
- Implement light/dark theme switching via tokens only.
- Verify contrast ratios meet WCAG AA for text and key data marks against both backgrounds.

Done when: tokens are published as a single module, both themes render, and a contrast check passes for the palette and axis labels.

tasks.name: 3.2 Build core chart primitives (time series, bar, distribution)
tasks.details:
Deliverable: three reusable primitive chart components behind a consistent props API.

Work:
- Time series chart: line and area variants, time axis with adaptive tick density, optional threshold band for SLO lines, gap handling for missing buckets.
- Bar chart: vertical/horizontal, grouped and stacked, sensible handling of many categories.
- Distribution chart: histogram for latency percentiles plus a categorical breakdown variant.
- Shared behaviors: tooltip, legend, empty state, and a 1000-point downsampling guard so charts stay responsive.
- Keep each component presentational: data in, no fetching.

Done when: each primitive renders correctly against fixture data at desktop and mobile widths, with no layout overflow.

tasks.name: 3.3 Build composite widgets (KPI tile, filter bar, sortable table)
tasks.details:
Deliverable: the higher-level widgets that compose the primitives into dashboard building blocks.

Work:
- KPI tile: headline value, delta vs. previous period, sparkline, and a neutral state when there is no prior data.
- Filter bar: date-range picker, segment/service multi-select, and a clear-all action, all driven by controlled state passed in by the parent.
- Data table: column sorting, pagination, numeric right-alignment, and a sticky header.
- Consistent loading skeleton and error state for every widget.
- Widgets emit intent (onFilterChange) and stay free of data fetching.

Done when: widgets compose into a sample grid with mock data, sorting and filtering update the table correctly, and loading/empty/error states are all demonstrable.

tasks.name: 3.4 Accessibility & responsive pass + component preview page
tasks.details:
Deliverable: an accessibility/responsiveness hardening pass and a preview page that documents every component.

Work:
- Keyboard navigation for interactive widgets (filter bar, table, legends).
- ARIA roles/labels for charts plus a text summary alternative (charts are not screen-reader accessible on their own).
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion and avoid relying on color alone to encode meaning.
- Verify layout at three breakpoints (mobile / tablet / desktop).
- Build the preview page rendering every primitive and widget against fixture data.

Done when: every component is on the preview page at all three breakpoints, an automated axe scan reports no critical issues, and keyboard-only navigation reaches all controls.

tasks.name: 4.1 Implement metrics query/API layer
tasks.details:
Deliverable: a read API the dashboard UI calls for both customer and log data.

Work:
- Endpoints: customer aggregates (counts by segment/cohort/date), log metrics (series by window), and a combined endpoint for the blended view.
- Uniform request contract: date range, granularity, segment filter, service filter.
- Validate and clamp inputs (reject inverted ranges, cap maximum window).
- Cache responses keyed on the full query signature with a short TTL.
- Return consistent error envelopes the UI can render.

Done when: contract tests cover every endpoint for happy path, empty result, invalid range, and a cache hit, and p95 response time is under 300ms on fixture data.

tasks.name: 4.2 Compose customer overview screen
tasks.details:
Deliverable: the customer-facing dashboard screen built from the Milestone 3 components.

Work:
- Layout: KPI row (total customers, new in period, churn estimate), growth time series, segment breakdown, and a sortable customer table.
- Wire each widget to the 4.1 customer endpoints through a shared data-fetch hook (loading/error surfaced per widget).
- Handle the sparse-data case gracefully (new install with one day of data).
- Ensure the screen has a defined empty state and a retry action on failure.

Done when: the screen renders from real ingested CSV data, every widget shows an independent loading and error state, and the table respects the active date range.

tasks.name: 4.3 Compose log health screen & combined view
tasks.details:
Deliverable: the log-health screen and the blended customer+log screen.

Work:
- Log health: error-rate time series with SLO threshold band, volume chart, latency percentile distribution, top error messages table.
- Combined view: correlate customer signups against error-rate and latency on a shared time axis with aligned buckets.
- Add drill-down from a top error message into a filtered view of that message.
- Make it explicit when two series have different granularity so the combined chart is not misleading.

Done when: both screens render from aggregate data, the shared time axis aligns correctly across sources, and drill-down produces a correctly filtered result.

tasks.name: 4.4 Global filters, URL state & resilience states
tasks.details:
Deliverable: cross-screen filter state that survives reloads and deep links.

Work:
- Single source of truth for filter state (date range, segment, service, granularity) hoisted to a shared provider.
- Serialize state to the URL query string so a view is shareable and back/forward navigation works.
- Debounce filter changes and cancel in-flight requests that a newer filter supersedes.
- Consistent loading skeletons, empty states with guidance, and error states with retry across all screens.

Done when: applying a filter updates every widget on every screen, copying the URL into a fresh tab reproduces the exact view, and rapidly toggling filters never renders a stale response.

tasks.name: 5.1 Unit & integration test suite for parsers, aggregations, API
tasks.details:
Deliverable: automated coverage of the risky logic.

Work:
- Golden-file tests for the CSV reader and log parser against committed fixtures.
- Property-style tests for normalization (dates, enums, numeric parsing) covering malformed input.
- Integration tests for aggregation correctness, including percentile merging and idempotent re-runs.
- Contract tests for all API endpoints from task 4.1.
- Publish a coverage report with an enforced threshold.

Done when: the suite runs in CI in under 10 minutes, covers every parser/aggregation module, and the coverage gate fails the build when it regresses.

tasks.name: 5.2 Seeded end-to-end smoke test
tasks.details:
Deliverable: one end-to-end test proving the whole chain works from file to rendered chart.

Work:
- Build a seed script that generates a deterministic CSV set and log archive (fixed random seed) with known expected totals.
- Run the full path: ingest CSV -> parse logs -> aggregate -> serve API -> load dashboard screens.
- Assert on visible KPI values against the seed's known totals.
- Keep the seed small enough to run per-commit (under 3 minutes).
- Capture screenshots on failure for triage.

Done when: the smoke test passes locally and in CI from a clean checkout with no manual setup steps.

tasks.name: 5.3 CI pipeline with build, lint & test gates
tasks.details:
Deliverable: a CI pipeline that blocks merges on broken code.

Work:
- Pipeline stages: install (cached), lint/format check, type check, unit+integration tests, e2e smoke, build.
- Run on pull requests and on main; publish coverage and test artifacts.
- Fail fast ordering so cheap checks run first.
- Add dependency and secret scanning.
- Document how to run the same checks locally in one command.

Done when: a deliberately broken PR is blocked by each gate, and CI wall-clock time for the common path is under 15 minutes.

tasks.name: 5.4 Deployment config, runbook & onboarding docs
tasks.details:
Deliverable: the ability to deploy and operate the dashboard without tribal knowledge.

Work:
- Environment configuration (dev/staging/prod) with secrets handled outside the repo.
- Container/build config for the API and the web app; one-command deploy to staging.
- Runbook: how to run an ingestion job, interpret a reconciliation report, backfill aggregates, and roll back a bad deploy.
- Data dictionary covering customer fields and log metrics, including known limitations from task 2.1.

Done when: a one-command deploy reaches staging from a clean environment, and someone unfamiliar with the system can run an ingest and a backfill using only the runbook.
